programme: VDR and SREBF1 set opposing arms of a nuclear-receptor-controlled sterol/lipid homeostasis module. VDR's target set includes INSIG2 (the ER-retention brake on SCAP/SREBP maturation) alongside CYP3A4, CYP24A1, ABCC3 and APOA1 — vitamin-D catabolism, xenobiotic clearance and lipid-transport genes that constrain lipid accumulation. SREBF1 (SREBP-1) is the opposing lipogenic/cholesterogenic driver, transactivating FASN, ACACA, LDLR, SCARB1, CETP, APOA2, PCK1 and STAR. Together VDR and SREBF1 act as a brake-and-driver pair setting how much sterol/lipid synthesis a cell runs.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, cholesterol and lipid handling is central to amyloid processing (raft-dependent APP cleavage) and glial lipid trafficking; VDR is placed here directly by three retrieved papers (vitamin-D-receptor modulation of amyloid pathology and neuronal/mitochondrial dynamics, and a genotype-linked drug-response study), and SREBF1 by three more (multiomics AD architecture, microglial-oxysterol-driven astrocyte lipid/ApoE secretion, and tau-aggregation-inhibitor mechanism).
role_in_b: In clear cell renal carcinoma, SREBF1-driven lipogenesis and lipophagy is the documented molecular basis of the lipid-droplet accumulation that gives the tumor its defining 'clear cell' morphology and supports tumor growth (PMID 37927089). VDR's role here is not directly evidenced in this record beyond a general Open Targets association (percentile 0.71) and an ambiguous prostate/kidney search hit.
shared_axis: Both tissues depend on the same VDR-restrained, SREBF1-driven balance of sterol/lipid synthesis: neurons and glia need it for membrane and amyloid-processing lipid pools, while ccRCC cells (reprogrammed downstream of VHL/HIF loss) need it to build the lipid stores that define the tumor. The same regulatory pair being load-bearing in each tissue's lipid economy, rather than any documented cross-talk between the diseases, is what would produce convergent detection of this module.
reasoning: Both carrying factors are independently placed by direct citations — VDR and SREBF1 in AD, SREBF1 additionally in ccRCC with a mechanism-specific paper — and the module (a brake/driver sterol-synthesis pair) is nameable from the factors' own target genes without invoking outside biology. No source states the two diseases share this axis, so the pairing rests on each disease's independent, well-evidenced involvement rather than a stated fact about this pair, capping the verdict at supported rather than established.
support: PMID 41335161 — VDR modulates neuronal/mitochondrial dynamics in an AD model; PMID 41910814 — vitamin D/VDR attenuates AD-like amyloid pathology; PMID 39112893 — VDR genotype affects rivastigmine response in AD patients; PMID 41422555 — SREBF1 appears in multiomics AD genetic/epigenetic architecture; PMID 36849076 — SREBF1-linked lipid metabolism/ApoE secretion in astrocytes relevant to AD; PMID 36918909 — SREBF1 pathway implicated in a tau-aggregation-inhibitor mechanism; PMID 37927089 — SREBF1/SREBP-1 regulates lipid synthesis and lipophagy to sustain lipid homeostasis in clear cell RCC.
how_to_falsify: In an AD model (e.g., APP/PS1 neurons or astrocytes) and in a ccRCC cell line, activate VDR (calcitriol) and measure INSIG2 induction plus SREBF1 target genes (FASN, ACACA, LDLR) and lipid-droplet content; the account predicts VDR activation should suppress SREBP1 output and lipid accumulation in both systems. If VDR activation leaves SREBF1 target expression and lipid accumulation unchanged in either tissue, the proposed coupling does not hold.
caveats: Brain and kidney are anatomically unrelated, so any shared axis must be argued mechanistically rather than assumed from tissue proximity. The 120 patient-group comparisons come from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so concordance counts (VDR 106/120, SREBF1 74/120) reflect repeated within-cohort comparisons more than broad independent replication — treat the counts as suggestive, not as 120 independent confirmations. CDX1 (82/120) lists VDR itself as a target, hinting at an upstream node, but no paper here places CDX1 in either disease and it was left out of the carrying set for that reason. The single-view exclusions (DNMT3L, TFAM, KLF14, etc.) and tissue-generic exclusions (SOX10, NOTCH1, NR3C1, etc.) do not overlap with the lipid-homeostasis story, so their removal does not appear to have hollowed out this account by coincidence.
